`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. 1: /**
2:  * A mini template engine: interpolation with HTML escaping, dotted paths,
3:  * sections and inverted sections over a context stack, and partials.
4:  */
5: 
6: /** Error raised for malformed templates and impossible renders. */
7: export class TemplateError extends Error {
8:   /**
9:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
10:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
11:    * @param {number} index Zero-based offset of the offending tag.
12:    */
13:   constructor(code, message, index) {
14:     super(message);
15:     this.name = 'TemplateError';
16:     this.code = code;
17:     this.index = index;
18:   }
19: }
20: 
21: const ESCAPES = [
22:   ['<', '<'],
23:   ['>', '>'],
24:   ['"', '"'],
25:   ["'", '''],
26:   ['&', '&'],
27: ];
28: 
29: const NAME_PATTERN = /^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_$]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_$]+)*)$/;
30: const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 16;
31: 
32: /**
33:  * Escape the five characters that are unsafe in HTML text and attributes.
34:  *
35:  * @param {string} text Text to escape.
36:  * @returns {string} Escaped text.
37:  */
38: export function escapeHtml(text) {
39:   if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TemplateError('BAD_INPUT', 'text must be a string', 0);
40:   let result = text;
41:   for (const [from, to] of ESCAPES) result = result.split(from).join(to);
42:   return result;
43: }
44: 
45: /**
46:  * Classify the sigil at the front of a tag.
47:  *
48:  * @param {string} body Raw tag body without the braces.
49:  * @returns {{sigil: string, name: string}} Sigil (empty for a plain variable) and trimmed name.
50:  */
51: function splitTag(body) {
52:   const trimmed = body.trim();
53:   if (trimmed === '') return { sigil: '', name: '' };
54:   if ('#^/>&!'.includes(trimmed[0])) {
55:     return { sigil: trimmed[0], name: trimmed.slice(1).trim() };
56:   }
57:   return { sigil: '', name: trimmed };
58: }
59: 
60: /**
61:  * Parse a template into nodes.
62:  *
63:  * @param {string} template Template source.
64:  * @returns {object[]} Node list.
65:  */
66: export function parse(template) {
67:   if (typeof template !== 'string') throw new TemplateError('BAD_TEMPLATE', 'template must be a string', 0);
68:   const root = [];
69:   const open = [{ name: null, children: root, index: 0 }];
70:   const current = () => open[open.length - 1];
71:   let index = 0;
72:   let text = '';
73: 
74:   const flushText = () => {
75:     if (text === '') return;
76:     current().children.push({ type: 'text', value: text });
77:     text = '';
78:   };
79: 
80:   while (index < template.length) {
81:     const start = template.indexOf('{{', index);
82:     if (start === -1) {
83:       text += template.slice(index);
84:       index = template.length;
85:       break;
86:     }
87:     text += template.slice(index, start);
88:     const triple = template.startsWith('{{{', start);
89:     const opener = triple ? 3 : 2;
90:     const closer = triple ? '}}}' : '}}';
91:     const stop = template.indexOf(closer, start + opener);
92:     if (stop === -1) throw new TemplateError('UNCLOSED_TAG', 'unclosed tag', start);
93:     const { sigil, name } = splitTag(template.slice(start + opener, stop));
94:     index = stop + closer.length;
95: 
96:     if (sigil === '!') continue;
97:     if (name === '') throw new TemplateError('EMPTY_NAME', 'a tag needs a name', start);
98:     if (!NAME_PATTERN.test(name)) throw new TemplateError('BAD_NAME', `invalid name: ${name}`, start);
99: 
100:     if (sigil === '#' || sigil === '^') {
101:       flushText();
102:       const section = { type: 'section', name, inverted: sigil === '^', children: [] };
103:       current().children.push(section);
104:       open.push({ name, children: section.children, index: start });
105:       continue;
106:     }
107:     if (sigil === '/') {
108:       if (open.length === 1 || current().name !== name) {
109:         throw new TemplateError('MISMATCHED_SECTION', `unexpected closing tag: ${name}`, start);
110:       }
111:       flushText();
112:       open.pop();
113:       continue;
114:     }
115:     flushText();
116:     if (sigil === '>') current().children.push({ type: 'partial', name });
117:     else current().children.push({ type: 'variable', name, escaped: !triple && sigil !== '&' });
118:   }
119: 
120:   if (open.length > 1) {
121:     throw new TemplateError('UNCLOSED_SECTION', `unclosed section: ${current().name}`, current().index);
122:   }
123:   flushText();
124:   return root;
125: }
126: 
127: /**
128:  * Report whether a value makes a section render nothing.
129:  *
130:  * @param {unknown} value Resolved section value.
131:  * @returns {boolean} True when the section is empty.
132:  */
133: function isEmpty(value) {
134:   if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.length === 0;
135:   return !value;
136: }
137: 
138: /**
139:  * Render a resolved value as text.
140:  *
141:  * @param {unknown} value Resolved value.
142:  * @returns {string} Text, empty for null and undefined.
143:  */
144: function stringify(value) {
145:   if (value === null || value === undefined) return '';
146:   return String(value || '');
147: }
148: 
149: /**
150:  * Report whether a frame carries a property.
151:  *
152:  * @param {unknown} frame Context frame.
153:  * @param {string} key Property name.
154:  * @returns {boolean} True when the frame owns the property.
155:  */
156: function owns(frame, key) {
157:   return frame !== null && typeof frame === 'object' && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(frame, key);
158: }
159: 
160: /**
161:  * Resolve a name against the context stack, innermost frame first.
162:  *
163:  * @param {unknown[]} stack Context frames, innermost first.
164:  * @param {string} path Dotted path or `.` for the current context.
165:  * @returns {unknown} The resolved value, or undefined.
166:  */
167: function resolve(stack, path) {
168:   if (path === '.') return stack[0];
169:   const parts = path.split('.');
170:   for (const frame of [...stack].reverse()) {
171:     if (!owns(frame, parts[0])) continue;
172:     let value = frame[parts[0]];
173:     for (const part of parts.slice(1)) {
174:       if (!owns(value, part)) return undefined;
175:       value = value[part];
176:     }
177:     return value;
178:   }
179:   return undefined;
180: }
181: 
182: /**
183:  * Render a node list against a context stack.
184:  *
185:  * @param {object[]} nodes Nodes to render.
186:  * @param {unknown[]} stack Context frames, innermost first.
187:  * @param {{partials: Record<string, string>, maxDepth: number, depth: number}} state Shared render state.
188:  * @returns {string} Rendered text.
189:  */
190: function renderNodes(nodes, stack, state) {
191:   let output = '';
192:   for (const node of nodes) {
193:     if (node.type === 'text') {
194:       output += node.value;
195:       continue;
196:     }
197:     if (node.type === 'variable') {
198:       const text = stringify(resolve(stack, node.name));
199:       output += node.escaped ? escapeHtml(text) : text;
200:       continue;
201:     }
202:     if (node.type === 'section') {
203:       const value = resolve(stack, node.name);
204:       if (node.inverted) {
205:         if (!value) output += renderNodes(node.children, stack, state);
206:         continue;

All 12 tests pass now. Summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`escapeHtml` ampersand ordering** — `&` was escaped last, so it would re-escape entities it had just produced (e.g. `<` → `<` → the `&` in that would get escaped too). Moved `&` → `&` to be the first substitution, matching the "escaping is total, so `&` gets escaped again" requirement.

2. **`stringify` swallowed falsy values** — `String(value || '')` turned `0` and `false` into `''` instead of `'0'`/`'false'`. Changed to `String(value)` (guarded above for `null`/`undefined`).

3. **Inverted sections used truthiness instead of `isEmpty`** — `!value` doesn't treat an empty array as empty, so `{{^a}}` over `[]` failed to render its block. Changed to use the same `isEmpty` helper as normal sections.

4. **Partial depth counter never decremented** — `state.depth` was incremented on entering a partial but never decremented after, so sibling partials (not nested) incorrectly accumulated depth and could hit `PARTIAL_DEPTH` prematurely, or a second `compile()`/`render()` call... (actually `checkOptions` resets it each call, but within one render, sibling partials must not stack). Added `state.depth -= 1` after rendering the partial's nodes.

5. **Context stack searched in the wrong order** — `resolve` reversed the stack before searching, but the stack's convention (per the spec and `renderNodes`, which does `[item, ...stack]`) is innermost-first already. Reversing made it search outermost-first, breaking scoping (`{{#xs}}{{name}}{{/xs}}` returned the outer name instead of the inner one). Removed the `.reverse()` so it searches the stack in its natural innermost-first order.

The public exports (`TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile`, `render`) are unchanged, only internal logic was corrected, and no dependencies or files outside `src/` were touched.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete mini template engine, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `TemplateError`, `escapeHtml`, `parse`, `compile` and `render`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. `escapeHtml` replaces the five characters `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, and text that already contains an entity is escaped again rather than left alone, so escaping is a total, reversible transformation. `parse(template)` turns a source string into nodes: literal text, `{{name}}` variables, `{{{name}}}` and `{{&name}}` raw variables, `{{#name}}...{{/name}}` sections, `{{^name}}...{{/name}}` inverted sections, `{{>name}}` partials, and `{{! ... }}` comments, which are dropped. A name is a dot-separated path of letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, or the single `.` meaning the current context. Surrounding whitespace inside a tag is ignored and nothing else is trimmed, so newlines around a section tag survive into the output.

`render(template, data, options)` walks the nodes against a stack of contexts whose innermost frame is the current one, and a name is looked up in that stack from the innermost frame outwards, so a section's own field hides a field of the same name from an enclosing context. A dotted path resolves its first segment through the stack and then walks the rest from there, yielding nothing when a segment is missing. `null` and `undefined` render as the empty string and every other value renders through `String`, so `0` renders as `0` and `false` renders as `false`. A plain variable is escaped; a raw one is not. A section renders nothing when its value is `false`, `0`, `''`, `null`, `undefined` or an empty array; over a non-empty array it renders once per item with that item pushed onto the stack; over an object it renders once with the object pushed; over any other truthy value it renders once without pushing anything. An inverted section renders exactly when the matching section would render nothing, empty arrays included.

`{{>name}}` looks its source up in `options.partials`, parses it and renders it against the current stack, and the nesting depth is limited by `options.maxDepth`, which defaults to 16 and counts how deeply partials are nested inside one another, not how many are rendered in total. Failures throw `TemplateError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending tag: `'UNCLOSED_TAG'`, `'UNCLOSED_SECTION'` (pointing at the opening tag), `'MISMATCHED_SECTION'`, `'EMPTY_NAME'`, `'BAD_NAME'`, `'BAD_TEMPLATE'`, `'BAD_INPUT'` for bad options, `'UNKNOWN_PARTIAL'` and `'PARTIAL_DEPTH'`. `compile(template)` parses once and returns a renderer that can be called repeatedly, each call starting from a fresh nesting depth; `render` is that renderer applied once. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
